items.english: It is a heat unknown in recent years. Wherever one looks, the roof-tiles of the mud-plastered houses reflect the sunlight dully, like lead, so that even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seem, at this rate, like to steam the chicks and eggs within to death just as they are. What is more, every field that is a field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the rising heat from the earth, and there is not one thing that, for all its greenness, is not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, too, whether from the warm vapours of these last days, the air near the ground, though clear, hangs thick and turbid, and here and there the piled clouds, like hail parched in an earthen pan, mere shapes, float in knobs. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who in this weather have gone out of their way to be upon a threshing-floor in the blazing sun.

Strangely, one of them lies stark naked on his back on the bare ground. What is more, for some reason or other, hand and foot he is wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself shows no sign of suffering it as a hardship. He is short, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, a man fat as a pig. Then a handy unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow, but what is inside that, too, is not known.
